body:
Although the benefits of `get_platform_specific_sdpa` are not very clear, which is due to we are focusing to get the infrastructure PR merged ASAP without enabling all tests, but in some cases we do.

The current UT has an assumption: "If a platform supports Flash Attention, it must support Memory efficient attention as well". However this is not true for ROCM (and potentially other platforms). 
`get_platform_specific_sdpa` is introduced to address this problem in a single place, and it will replace more `@parametrize("kernel")` when we are enabling more tests.

Additionally there is another benefit. If a new type of attention backend were added, only this function needs updates.

After checking the logic of `check_submodules` it seems impractical to check out submodules according to the build types. In latest versions the value `USE_ROCM` is determined by cmake and stored in `CMakeCache.txt`, but this file is not available until calling `build_caffe2`, which happens after `check_submodules`. Thus `check_submodules` cannot tell the current build target and only check out `triton-mathaot/` for `USE_ROCM`, because its value is still unknown.

Nevertheless we made another improvement by removing unused nested submodules in `triton-mathaot`, and set the `shadow = true` for this submodule. These two efforts cut the size of `.git/modules/third_party/triton-mathaot` down to 31MB
I think this should be an error not a warn no?

@malfet More specifically, this is the call order:
```
    check_submodules()
    check_pydep("yaml", "pyyaml")

    build_caffe2(
        version=version,
        cmake_python_library=cmake_python_library,
        build_python=True,
        rerun_cmake=RERUN_CMAKE,
        cmake_only=CMAKE_ONLY,
        cmake=cmake,
    )
```

The `build_caffe2` call will configure CMake via the `cmake.generate` call, which will provide the `cmake.get_cmake_cache_variables()` method for us to query if `USE_ROCM` is `True`. That is how subsequent code in `configure_extension_build` refers to CMake variables via `cmake_cache_vars`.
